input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure the served volume V_lab (m3) of /habitat/lab as V = Qe * tau, from a rise at reduced scrubber speed then a decay at full speed, occupants' CO2 as the source.

monitoring.reason: The two occupants of the lab breathe the raised CO2; they are also the test's CO2 source and must stay in the lab.

steps.why: Rise: reduce effective flow to 0.3 m3/min so lab CO2 climbs from 1300 ppm towards a higher equilibrium (about 2500 ppm for 2 awake occupants). Hatch closed, held closed.
Decay: full speed (Qe = 1 m3/min), record CO2 falling towards its equilibrium; fit C(t)=C_eq+(C0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau). Hatch unchanged.

abort.when: the device refuses a step's speed command
FE-2 or CDR outside 45-120 bpm, monitoring lost, or one more person enters/leaves the lab

expected.rise: Step 1 (Qe 0.3 m3/min): lab CO2 rises monotonically from 1300 ppm, by roughly 250-300 ppm over 25 min (about +270 ppm to ~1570 ppm if V is near the 30 m3 first guess, tau_rise ~ V/Qe ~ 100 min, C_eq ~ 2500 ppm from G = 2 x 0.38 L/min / 0.3 m3/min). Stays under 2500 ppm.
expected.decay: Step 2 (Qe 1 m3/min): CO2 falls towards C_eq ~ 760 ppm (G/Qe), tau ~ V/Qe ~ 30 min for V ~ 30 m3; expect roughly 500 ppm fall in 30 min. V_lab = Qe * tau, expected in the 10-200 m3 fitted range, about 30 m3 (first guess, stated as such). The two phases give consistent V within ~15 percent.
expected.disproof: Hypotheses fail if: hab-b CO2 (co2-2) moves with the lab's during the test (hatch closed still exchanges air: design 3 m3/min per station-topology); the fitted C_eq differs from G/Qe by more than ~20 percent or the fit residuals are systematic (not well mixed / source not steady); rise and decay give V differing by more than ~30 percent (Qe not as the datasheet, or the lag of 3.33 min not accounted); starting CO2 of 1300 ppm already above the 760 ppm full-speed equilibrium suggests exchange with hab-b, a lower current speed or a higher source than assumed. In those cases V_lab is only an effective volume, not the room's.

hypotheses: The lab is one well-mixed zone; the hatch to hab-b is held closed in both steps and the residual exchange through it (design 3 m3/min per station-topology) is not measured, only observed via the co2-2 record in hab-b.
The two occupants stay in the lab, awake and at steady activity (0.38 L/min each, band 0.26-0.45); the source is not measured, only assumed from the library.
Effective flow scales linearly with speed: Qe = 1 m3/min x speed/100 (datasheet), with a 3.33 min lag after each speed change that is excluded from the fit.

Rise phase (25 min) is shorter than one time constant (~100 min at 30 percent speed) because of the 60 min cap; the rise only has to exceed sensor noise, and tau is taken mainly from the decay phase (30 min, ~1 tau).
Volume V_lab is a first guess of 30 m3 (register default), used only to size the durations.
